addendum_hash_recipe.note: Recompute from this committed file alone; depends on every field except addendum_hash.

amendment_rule: Sealed before the first effective freeze instant; governs only forecasts frozen at or after it. Any further change is another dated addendum.
not_covered: The retired MC-forecast family (SOL v1 cohorts) keeps its sealed rule for the cohorts it still governs: their verdicts continue to report coverage misses and are not re-tiered. SOL v2 (BBM tier family) is not listed: its claims are binary tier claims already judged on every OK-tier breach (ok_false_safe, missed_severe), with no near-certain exclusion.
title: Breach-probability family addendum 1: confident calls count (a near-certain forecast that is wrong is now tested)

what_changes.evaluation_order: Unchanged: INVALID, then EVIDENCE AGAINST (now including confident_calls), then CALIBRATED, else UNTESTED. A fired confident_calls trigger therefore also blocks CALIBRATED.
what_changes.new_against_trigger: confident_calls: EVIDENCE AGAINST if, for ANY group (the standard's own groups: band widths, the XRPL lose / lose1 events, the grid's p-bins) and EITHER side - CONFIDENT-SAFE items (p < low_max) or CONFIDENT-BREACH items (p > high_min) - frozen on or after the standard's effective_from_freeze_day: the side has >= min_items resolved items, the stream has >= min_matured_days matured freeze days since the effective day, the side's gap = mean(outcome - p) is WRONG-WAY by at least min_abs_gap (safe side: gap >= +min_abs_gap, the outcome happened more than claimed; breach side: gap <= -min_abs_gap), and the ci block-bootstrap interval of that gap excludes 0 on the wrong-way side. Resampling is the standard's own: whole freeze days in moving blocks of block_days, resamples draws, seed = the standard's seed + seed_offset.
what_changes.reported_not_gated: Every verdict reports, per group and side since the effective day: n, outcomes, expected outcomes (sum of p), gap and the interval - whether or not the trigger can fire yet.

what_does_not_change: Everything else in each standard: forecast objects, outcomes, informative-item calibration tests and their thresholds, INVALID battery, CALIBRATED conditions, cadence, models. Items frozen BEFORE a standard's effective day are never tested by this trigger - it is not applied to any outcome or forecast that existed when it was sealed.
why: Every standard listed tests calibration only on 'informative' items (0.02 <= p <= 0.98); near-certain forecasts are shown in the reliability table but never gated. So a stream whose 'will not break' calls (p < 0.02) break often, or whose 'will break' calls (p > 0.98) do not, could never be judged wrong on that - the same blind spot that let the retired SOL v1 cohorts read UNTESTED under the MC-forecast standing standard while 5, 7, 9 and 11 of 23 realized outcomes fell outside their forecast ranges. The confident call is the claim a user leans on hardest ('safe to hold'), so it must be falsifiable.
